text:
inc-bot: Incident alert: GPU pool 'inference-prod-north' reporting sustained queue growth > 95% and HPA failed to add replicas for 12m. Pager duty: @sylvia is on-call.

sylvia: I'm on it. seeing 4k queued requests, 500ms->3s tail lat, and a bunch of 429 throttles in the logs. paging customers now.

mike: thanks. initial hunch: metrics pipeline to the HPA adapter is lagging. prom-adapter logs show 504s and `metrics-server` connection timeouts.

arjun: confirming from ML side: many requests are to the gpu-large model (gptx-4L). queue growth correlates to a failed scale around 1749989400.

janet: customer-ops: we already have 2 customer reports of degraded latency and timeouts. adding a public incident banner for affected customers (small subset in eu-north).

lisa: quick ask: can we route requests to smaller model variants as temporary mitigation? dev teams need a plan for live mitigation.

sylvia: Plan A: try to force HPA recompute and bump pods manually; Plan B: temporarily route traffic to cpu-fallback or smaller gpu pool; Plan C: provision extra dedicated GPUs if needed.

mike: digging into k8s: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` shows target metrics stale: `lastScaleTime` 12m ago, `currentReplicas=8`, `desiredReplicas=8`. adapter metrics: `prometheus_adapter_query_latency_ms` spikes and `queue_length` metric ingestion lag.

sylvia: executing manual scale up for deployment inference-gpu-svc to +4 replicas now:```bash
kubectl scale deployment/inference-gpu-svc --replicas=12 -n inference
```

arjun: note: scaling will help but slower because pod boot + model load ~3-5m per pod. pushing smaller-model routing asap.

mike: also seeing `metrics-server` returning "connection refused" from `metrics-server-0` pods. restarting metrics-server pod to reestablish node metrics.```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-server -n kube-system
```

sylvia: restarted metrics-server, restarting prometheus-adapter as well.```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter -n monitoring
```

devex-bot: Deploy bot: prometheus-adapter rollout started at 1749990123 by @sylvia.

mike: adapter restart logs show upstream scrape backlog cleared, adapter now returning metrics for HPA. HPA responds and desiredReplicas jumped to 18. Good.

arjun: rolling traffic to smaller model via routing rule:```yaml
- match: model=="gptx-4L"
  route: model=="gptx-4L-small"  # temporary
  weight: 100
``` applied to canary route.

sylvia: applied - redirected 40% of traffic to small variant to reduce load while pods warm. tail lat improved slightly.

janet: customers notified: banner updated, posting ETA 30m. no large-scale data loss, only timeouts and degraded latency.

lisa: thanks team. postmortem reminders: capture root cause (adapter/metrics-server failure), why HPA didn't fallback earlier, and if autoscaler retry/poll interval needs tuning.

mike: suspected root cause: metrics-server OOM from recent node upgrade causing adapter scrape failures -> adapter queue backlog -> HPA saw stale metrics and didn't scale. need to check node kubelet logs + node kubelet auth failure around 1749988800.

arjun: mitigation checklist: 1) route to smaller models, 2) manual scale, 3) restart metrics components, 4) provision warm standby GPUs for faster scaling.

sylvia: doing a controlled uncordon/scale on extra gpu nodes in eu-north (spinning up reserved capacity). provisioning ticket created: #PCI-3421.

devex-bot: Infra action: new dedicated-gpu instance pool being provisioned (request id p-9082).

janet: customer-ops: holding banner until latency steady 75th pctl within SLO. will update in 15m.

mike: monitoring shows HPA stabilizing at 16-18 replicas, queued requests starting to drain, 429 rate falling.

arjun: model-fallback reduced 429s by ~60% in first 6m. still seeing some longer tails for big requests.

sylvia: marking incident as mitigated at 1749990360. moving to post-incident review channel. Please document playbook gaps (metrics ingestion, adapter retries, HPA fallback thresholds).

lisa: I can lead the postmortem. assign owners and schedule a 45m postmortem within 24h. link stub created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1749990000-postmortem.

janet: final note for timeline: root cause likely metrics-server process instability after node kubelet rotation + adapter backlog; customer impact limited but real; next steps: increase adapter scrape parallelism, add local buffering for metrics, and pre-warm small GPU pool.

sylvia: thanks all. handing off to @lisa for postmortem and @mike/@arjun for remediation tasks. on-call clear. :thumbsup:
